items.title: Where did burnt cash from Justice Yashwant Varma’s residence vanish? Judge’s panel has no clear answer
items.summary: What happened to the ₹500 notes that were seen burning at the residence of Justice Yashwant Varma in March 2025? A three-member judges inquiry committee that probed the matter has not come out with any clear answers, due to the lack of conclusive evidence. However, the panel report does raise questions over the role of the judge’s staff in disappearance of the burnt cash. It reveals that the police failed to seize the burnt cash as there was no clear instruction to do so. The panel has said that non-seizure and absence of panchnama were lapses on part of the police officials present on the spot. It, however, attributed the lapses to the “sensitive” nature of the matter involving a then sitting judge of the Delhi High Court. “This lapse should be viewed in the light of the fact that this occurrence happened at the official residence of a Sitting Judge of a High Court and the police and fire officials were fully cognizant of this fact,” the panel said. items.title: Allegations against Justice Yashwant Varma proven: Judges' panel finds interference with evidence, no explanation for cash
items.summary: A three-member judges inquiry committee has found all three charges against Allahabad High Court Justice Yashwant Varma proved, including possession of substantial unexplained cash at his official residence, interference with material evidence and furnishing evasive and misleading explanations. The committee constituted by Lok Sabha speaker Om Birla tabled its report before the Lok Sabha on Wednesday, The inquiry concerned the discovery of burnt and partially burnt ₹500 notes following a fire at Justice Varma’s official residence in New Delhi, on the intervening night of March 14 and 15, 2025. Justice Varma was then a judge of the Delhi High Court. “ The committee therefore records its final findings that Articles of Charges I, II & III are proved, ” the report said. The committee was headed by Supreme Court judge Justice Aravind Kumar and included former Bombay High Court Chief Justice and now Supreme Court Justice Shree Chandrashekhar and Senior Advocate BV Acharya. items.title: Court can't create Section 377 IPC-like offence in BNS: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Wednesday remarked that it cannot "create" offences that existed under Section 377 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) but have been dropped in the Bharatiya Nagarik Sanhita (BNS). Section 377 IPC punished non-consensual intercourse "against the order of nature with any man, woman or animal". It provided punishment of up to 10 years. The current legal framework dropped the provision and the BNS provisions apply only where the perpetrator of a sexual offence is male and the victim is female. The petition before the Court said that there should be a gender-neutral interpretation of the BNS provisions. A Division Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia said that it is a legislative policy matter and can only be looked into by the legislature. “We understand your [petitioners'] anxiety, but these are legislative policy matters… The offence has to be described. Which is the authority that can do it? It’s the legislature. What can we do about it? Can we provide something which is not provided for by the legislature? items.title: Why are scammers getting Meta’s copyright protection tool but not creators? Delhi High Court asks
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Wednesday asked Meta why established content creators are denied access to Meta’s rights manager tool even as scammers appear to be able to use it to issue fraudulent copyright strikes against original content [Mohit Kumar v. John Doe/Ashok Kumar and Others]. Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani asked Meta to place on record its policy and eligibility criteria for granting access to rights manager, a free content-protection tool offered by the company. The Court also asked Meta to explain the basis on which applications for access to the tool are rejected. “ Why doesn’t everybody have access to it then? ” the Court asked. Anup Jairam Bhambhani The suit was filed by Mohit Kumar, an artificial intelligence, business and e-commerce coach who creates educational content on social media under the handle “Rise With Mohit”. Kumar alleged that scammers had downloaded his original videos and registered them with Meta’s rights manager as their own. They then allegedly used the tool to issue copyright strikes against Kumar’s accounts. Rights Manager identifies matching content uploaded on Facebook and Instagram. items.title: Russia appoints former CJI DY Chandrachud as arbitrator in dispute with Ukrainian bank
items.summary: Former Chief Justice of India (CJI) DY Chandrachud has been appointed by Russia as its arbitrator in an investment treaty dispute brought by Ukrainian state-owned bank Oschadbank. According to a report by Global Arbitration Review , Costa Rican arbitrator and former trade minister Dyalá Jiménez will preside over the three-member tribunal. Jiménez was jointly selected as president by both sides. The third arbitrator will be Greek arbitrator and National University of Singapore professor Stavros Brekoulakis who was appointed by Oschadbank. The arbitration has been initiated under the 1998 bilateral investment treaty between Ukraine and Russia. Oschadbank’s claim concerns assets and operations in the Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson and Zaporizhzhia regions that it claims it lost following Russia’s military actions in Ukraine, particularly after the full-scale invasion in 2022. The claim is understood to be worth hundreds of millions of dollars. Oschadbank initiated the proceedings after a notice of dispute served on Russia in July 2025 allegedly went unanswered. items.title: Detect, delete, deport — A humanitarian crisis in Bengaluru
items.summary: On August 8, 2026, police teams broke into the sheds of Bengali Muslim migrant workers around 6:30 am at various locations across Bengaluru, and detained over 900 people, including children and elderly. All of them are employed in manually collecting or segregating garbage – a job nobody else in the city is willing to do. Apparently, this action against the people who provide this lifeline service to the city, was taken to ‘identify illegal Bangladeshis’. The police carried no warrants or official orders for their so-called verification drive. They barged into their homes early in the morning, demanded to see documents and responded with physical aggression when their methods were questioned. Even when the workers produced their identity proof, the police dragged them away. Their phones were confiscated, and in some cases, their sheds were vandalised. The police even smashed some CCTV cameras that the workers had put up for their own safety in the settlements. The brazen, racially motivated violations by the law enforcement agencies continued even after human rights activists and lawyers convened. items.title: Hearings not taking place for years: Supreme Court flags serious concerns with consumer forums, seeks report
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday frowned upon the performance of consumer commissions across the country for the inordinate amount of time taken by them to decide consumer cases/ complaints. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also took note of a newspaper report which termed the performance of consumer forums as "pitiful and poor". In many pending matters, hearings do not take place for years, the Court noted. "The moment you start paying for case disposal, you will see how the disposal will multiply. The moment you keep on adding more and more infrastructure, the courts and facilities, then unfortunately this is the outcome. There is a newspaper report also in which the following issues have been highlighted with respect to the pitiful and poor performance of the Consumer Commissions, including the National Consumer Commission. The inordinate delay in disposal of the pending matters, especially when even hearings are not taking place for years," the Court said. items.title: Bowing to corporate pressure? Supreme Court slams FSSAI's reluctance to put warning labels on foods high in sugar, salt, fat
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday questioned the reluctance of the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) to introduce front-of-pack warning labels on packaged food products containing high levels of sugar, salt and saturated fat. A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and KV Viswanathan was hearing a case in which the Court had earlier urged the FSSAI to consider introducing such warning labels in the interest of public health. Today, the Court took critical note that the FSSAI was hesitant to implement such a measure, going by a the minutes of a meeting held by the food standards watchdog. The Court asked if the FSSAI was bowing down to corporate entities involved in food manufacture. " Are you taking the court for a toss? ... There is immense pressure at the end of all these corporate houses on you. And you are succumbing to that pressure! We are doing this in public interest. Keep it in mind. We are not doing it for ourselves. Why are you not abiding by our order? What have you done so far? We know the pressure on you.
